liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Cold Rain and Snow** (1 review): Commonly said to open the last set in rain, but this listener recalls sun emerging around Sugar Magnolia [15]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Reviewer's pick of the show is the Not Fade Away > Goin' Down the Road > Not Fade Away sequence [19]

## The recordings

- **gd1972-09-03.sbd.gems.101143.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 72 songs; 491 min; rated 3.33/5 by 6 [1]
- **gd1972-09-03.sbd.greenberg.powell.18779.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 34 songs; 246 min; rated 3.5/5 by 6 [2]
- **gd72-09-03.sbd.new.hanno.20168.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 32 songs; 249 min; rated 4.32/5 by 19 [3]. Said about its sound: Recording is not the cleanest, per the reviewer; Recording fails to capture the show's superb in-house sound from the Wall of Sound; Reviewer's cassette copy sounded horrible; quality is poor [8][11][12][14][17]
- **gd1972-09-03.166363.sbd.bear.gems.flac1648**: soundboard; 30 songs; 238 min; rated 3.75/5 by 4 [4]
- **gd1972-09-03.sbd.steinhaus-bunjes-teute.cotsman.13563.shnf**: soundboard; 32 songs; 248 min [5]. Said about its sound: Audience recording supplying first set is decent through Tennessee Jed, then poor, with many cuts at song starts [5]

## Around the show

- Typical late-summer Boulder afternoon thundershowers disrupted the stage; band joked about frisbees as rain hats and dried their piano [8]
- Bobby introduced the band's newest members, Keith and Donna, and pointed out an energy cloud over the stadium [11]
- Bobby remarked the crowd might want something straight, but the band never plays straight [11]
- Ticket cost $3; rain began briefly during the second-set China; free baggies of herb, papers and matches were thrown from stage [13]
- Soundboard portion runs 3 hours 14 minutes, plus 48 minutes of audience tracks for the first eight [18]
- Folsom Field appeared in the closing credits of Mork and Mindy [19]
- Tape ends with the band still on stage, suggesting at least one more tune [2]
- Reviewer suggests it could be the longest show of 1972, unverified [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1972-09-03.sbd.gems.101143.flac16**: transferred by Jamie Waddell; source: Composite sources: MR>cass, MR>cass>cass and multi generation sources [1]. Also: Part of the GEMS yardsale tapes project; patches and source changes are left for listeners to find [1]
- **gd1972-09-03.sbd.greenberg.powell.18779.shnf**: taped by See info file; transferred by See info file; source: Candellario MSR > P > D > CD plus Audience tapes [2]. Also: Soundboard patched with three unknown audience sources; Powell coordinated uploads and Greenberg did patches and mastering [2]
- **gd72-09-03.sbd.new.hanno.20168.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard and Audience composite [3]. Also: Reviewer's cassette sounded worse than the show; a later disc copy still lacks the first set; First eight tracks and the final track are audience recordings; the rest is soundboard [15][17]
- **gd1972-09-03.166363.sbd.bear.gems.flac1648**: taped by Augustus Owsley Stanley III (aka Bear); transferred by 2023 transfer and mastering by Jim Blackwood Speed/pitch adjusted by Jason Chastain Minor repairs, track, FLAC, and pack by Steve Gravel; source: SBD > Bear's Master Reels > Cassette [4]. Also: Bear-related GEMS soundboard source, aired on Tucson's KXCI Dead Air radio program, hosted by Jim Blackwood [4]
- **gd1972-09-03.sbd.steinhaus-bunjes-teute.cotsman.13563.shnf**: taped by Unknown; transferred by J. Cotsman; source: SBD > Master Reel [5]. Also: Bertha comes from the audience recording; a minor tape stoppage occurs in Bird Song [5]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Zaremba: [CoME Blog: Fifty Years Ago…Colorado’s First Cannabis “Dispensary”?](https://colomusic.org/blog/fifty-years-ago-colorados-first-cannabis-dispensary/) [21]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [current-page:url:arg:3 | Grateful Dead](https://www.dead.net/tags/boulder) [22]
